subject.kind: documentation: a how-to with reference parts
subject.purpose: lets a visitor pick a plugin, install it and start it from the page alone
subject.reader: a new visitor deciding on the plugins, who leaves or fails the install if a step is missing

promises.text: three plugins and what each one does
what each one needs on your machine

flaws: a visitor cannot tell from the top what each plugin is for
an install fails for a tool the page never named
a reader thinks all three must be installed together
a reader installs a plugin and cannot begin
a link or a path has gone stale
a pinned tag does not exist
a role or a tool has no meaning
a dense line hides its point
a diagram has no stated point

criteria.text: The opening paragraph says in one clause per plugin what teamwork, paperwork and homework each do.
criteria.from: Diátaxis how-to: a reader can follow it

criteria.text: The Installation section gives a marketplace-add command and one install command for each of the three plugins.
criteria.from: Diátaxis how-to: a reader can follow it
criteria.fix: Give one marketplace-add command and one install command per plugin.

criteria.text: A table states what each plugin needs on the machine (tools, accounts, versions).
criteria.from: Diátaxis how-to: a reader can follow it

criteria.text: The page states that each plugin works without the others.
criteria.from: Diátaxis how-to: a reader can follow it

criteria.text: Each plugin's section holds a usage example or a named command that starts it.
criteria.from: Diátaxis how-to: a reader can follow it

criteria.text: Each relative link in the page points to a file or folder that exists at the graded commit.
criteria.from: Diátaxis reference: it holds what a reader looks up
criteria.command: ! grep -oE '\]\([^)#]+' README.txt | cut -c3- | grep -v '^http' | while read -r path; do git cat-file -e "74b7410:$path" 2>/dev/null || echo "gone: $path"; done | grep gone
criteria.fix: Point each dead link at a path that exists.

criteria.text: Each file path the page writes in backticks with a plugin folder prefix exists at the graded commit.
criteria.from: Diátaxis reference: it holds what a reader looks up
criteria.command: ! grep -oE '`(teamwork|paperwork|homework)/[^` ]+`' README.txt | tr -d '`' | while read -r path; do git cat-file -e "74b7410:$path" 2>/dev/null || echo "gone: $path"; done | grep gone
criteria.fix: Correct each path that no longer exists.

criteria.text: The teamwork roles (owner, manager, worker, sentinel, judge) are each defined in one line before the usage example.
criteria.from: Diátaxis reference: it holds what a reader looks up

criteria.text: The marketplace-add command pins a version tag that exists in the repository.
criteria.from: Diátaxis how-to: a reader can follow it

criteria.text: Each required outside tool (herdr, uv, pele, Alloy, gh) has a link or a gloss at its first mention.
criteria.from: Diátaxis reference: it holds what a reader looks up
criteria.anchors: A link or a clause saying what the tool is counts as a gloss.

criteria.text: No prose line in the page is over 400 characters.
criteria.from: Diátaxis reference: it holds what a reader looks up

criteria.text: The page names its license and links the license file.
criteria.from: Diátaxis reference: it holds what a reader looks up
criteria.fix: Name the license and link LICENSE.

criteria.text: Each diagram sits under a one-sentence summary saying what it shows.
criteria.from: Diátaxis reference: it holds what a reader looks up
